#161825. Data centers are getting their own natural gas power plants

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1198 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Technologyreview ↗ Open Full Page

Data centers are getting their own natural gas power plants

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1198 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Technologyreview

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, one of the biggest roadblocks to starting up a data center is getting approval to connect to the electric grid—a wait that could last as long as a decade.
  • Sources indicate that xAI’s Memphis campus has famously used dozens of natural gas turbines, some of them without permits, as far back as 2024.
  • According to recent reports, as of October 2026, data center developers have announced intends for more than 100 behind-the-meter gas power plants at facilities in the US, according to data from Cleanview, a market intelligence manufacturer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, one of the biggest roadblocks to starting up a data center is getting approval to connect to the electric grid—a wait that could last as long as a decade. Some developers aren’t willing to wait and are instead opting to build their own off-grid, or behind-the-meter, gas power plants to fuel the AI boom.

Sources indicate that xAI’s Memphis campus has famously used dozens of natural gas turbines, some of them without permits, as far back as 2024. At the time, that facility was a rarity, and it faced scrutiny from regulators. It remains the subject of ongoing legal battles. But the strategy of going off-grid for power has since become a lot more common.

According to recent reports, as of October 2026, data center developers have announced intends for more than 100 behind-the-meter gas power plants at facilities in the US, according to data from Cleanview, a market intelligence manufacturer. The facilities have a combined planned capacity of over 115 gigawatts, more than double the peak power demand of California. The vast majority of these announcements have come since the beginning of 2025.

Sources indicate that it’s possible that not all these facilities will be built; only a small fraction are under construction or operating today. But there’s a growing trend of large data centers looking to build their own power supply, and this could shape the grid—and its climate impacts—for decades to come.

Recent findings suggest that building your own power plant is generally more expensive than just hooking up to the grid, but the AI rush has made developers willing to pay a significant premium to get online faster. “The biggest motivator for on-site power right now from data centers is speed,” indicates Musfika Mishi, an associate at BloombergNEF, an energy consultancy.

When developers want to build a new industrial facility—like a data center—that requires a lot of electricity, they need to request a grid connection from a local utility or regional grid operator. That request kicks off a yearslong process in which grid planners study the existing grid to understand what would need to be built to safely deliver power to the facility without compromising reliability. Upgrades might be required, like building new transmission lines or larger transformers, and the developer might be on the hook to help pay for them.

In a recent development, rather than waiting for that process to play out, developers can opt to instead build their own power plants. These facilities are referred to as “behind the meter” because they sit on the customer’s side of a utility meter—supplying the building directly, rather than relying on a utility via a grid hookup.

“This shift in the data center developers’ power strategies towards off-grid gas raises some important questions about how data centers will be powered going forward,” says Brendan Pierpont, director of electricity at the think tank Energy Innovation.

Behind-the-meter doesn’t always mean being totally disconnected from the grid, however. Some facilities may build such plants as a temporary measure, eventually connecting to the grid and tapping their own power plants only as backup. “It’s really just a very expensive way to bridge that maybe five-to-seven-year timeline gap until these data centers can get a grid connection,” Pierpont states.

Recent findings suggest that even if gas plants are pitched as a near-term solution, building new fossil fuel infrastructure could lead to longer-term effects, since an operator might choose to continue running plants once they’ve spent money building them. “Even though data centers say that it’s a grid-bridging solution, the probability that it is going to be in use much longer is a real risk, and that leads to fossil fuel lock-in,” Mishi notes.

It has been revealed that the on-site gas rush could have major implications for greenhouse-gas emissions. Today, the US grid is still reliant on fossil fuels, but nuclear and renewables together make up about 40% of electricity generation. That means making a grid connection is generally a lower-emissions option than relying entirely on an on-site gas plant. (That’s not the case everywhere—India, for example, is expecting to see a data center boom in the next decade, and its grid is largely served by emissions-intensive coal-fired power plants today.).

Utilities are already planning to build more natural gas power plants on the grid to meet rising electricity demand. Equipment manufacturers are struggling to keep up with the surge, and it’s pushing developers of behind-the-meter plants toward less-efficient alternatives.

Today, large natural gas plants generally use combined-cycle turbines. These capture heat to generate additional electricity, making them more efficient than single-cycle turbines, which are generally cheaper to build. Very few of the planned behind-the-meter facilities, however, will use combined-cycle turbines, Mishi says. That means these off-grid plants will likely produce more greenhouse-gas emissions than even other natural gas resources.

BloombergNEF is also tracking on-site natural gas plants at data centers, finding 181 gigawatts’ worth of unveiled projects globally, with 90% of that capacity designated for the US. If all planned behind-the-meter gas plants for data centers in the US go ahead, they could emit 345 million metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent each year by 2035, according to a BloombergNEF report. That’s 152 million metric tons more than if those data centers pulled power from the US grid—a difference greater than the total annual emissions of the Netherlands.

Recent findings suggest that and while it might seem logical that data centers bringing their own power could ease communities’ energy bills, those facilities going off-grid doesn’t protect prices for everyone else, says Matthias Fripp, director of global policy research at Energy Innovation. More demand for natural gas could push its price higher, he explains, which could in turn raise rates for the roughly 60% of American households that use natural gas for heating and cooking. That effect may also trickle into electricity prices.

It has been revealed that there’s still a lot of uncertainty about how much of this gas rush will come to fruition, so this future isn’t set in stone. Today, just 4.9 gigawatts of behind-the-meter gas projects tied to data centers are operating, and 15.8 gigawatts are under construction, according to Cleanview’s data.

Creative solutions could also help limit the climate burden of the on-site gas buildout, BloombergNEF’s Mishi says. Building gas alongside on-site renewables or energy storage could help limit how often a gas plant needs to fire up, she says, though the economics of building multiple energy sources can be tricky.

While the grid is struggling to keep up with demand, building more renewables could help, Fripp adds. In a recent study, his team found that building renewables and energy storage to meet rising electricity demand could be reliable and cheaper than relying on fossil fuels.

Industry observers note that “These data centers want a lot of power, and they want it fast, and the grid is not well equipped to provide that,” Fripp says. “There are potentially good solutions and bad solutions … Rushing off the grid and putting in your own behind-the-meter gas is probably a bad way, because it’s still going to raise other people’s bills, and it’s not great for the environment.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The official was reportedly convicted of passing on secret information in exchange for payment.
  • The report was published on an online account run by Gold Wall Press, a publisher tied to the National Administration of State Secrets Protection.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Chinese court has sentenced a government official to death for spying for a foreign country, according to a report published Monday by a state-linked social media account.

The official was reportedly convicted of passing on secret information in exchange for payment.

The report was published on an online account run by Gold Wall Press, a publisher tied to the National Administration of State Secrets Protection.

The report named the man only as Ma. The AFP news agency called him a ministerial official, while Reuters described him as an administrative official in China's central apparatus.

According to recent reports, according to the report, a foreign operative called "Kailin" recruited Ma while he worked overseas. Kailin first met him regularly on the pretext of learning Chinese. The talks then turned to politically sensitive topics.

A colleague of Kailin's later threatened to tell Chinese authorities about Ma's earlier disclosures unless he cooperated. Later, Ma signed an agreement committing him to confidentiality and loyalty. He received monthly payments and a laptop for sending and receiving intelligence, the report said.

Upon returning to China, Ma kept passing on information, sending more than 100 intelligence reports, 35 of them later deemed "top secret," the report stated. He was allegedly paid over one million yuan ($150,000, €138,000).

The sentence also includes confiscation of all his personal property.

The report did not say when or where Ma was sentenced, or whether he had already been executed.

Chinese courts rarely publish details of state security cases, but the secrecy regulator and the Ministry of State Security have increasingly publicized them as a warning to officials not to become spies.

"This shocking case serves as yet another wake-up call," the report mentioned.

In recent years, the US CIA has published videos in Mandarin seeking informants in China's bureaucracy and military, which Beijing has called a "damning confession.".

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    China on Tuesday unveiled the crew for this week's Shenzhou-24 space mission, with a Pakistani payload specialist set to become the first foreign astronaut to board its Tiangong space station.

    The China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) said that Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a 40-year-old former Pakistani air force pilot, would join two Chinese colleagues when the mission launches from the Jiuquan launch center in China's northwestern Gobi Desert at 8:18 a.m. local time (0018 GMT)  on Wednesday.

    "I carry the name of Pakistan on my shoulder, the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis," Ali told a news conference on Tuesday, switching between Urdu, Mandarin and English.

    "To every child who is watching while I'm in orbit, just look up at the sky and remember that I am up there with your dreams," he noted.

    To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

    Pakistani officials welcomed Ali's selection as a significant milestone in relations between Islamabad and Beijing who are this year marking 75 years of cooperation in space.

    Information Minister Attaullah Tarar described the mission as a "source of joy and pride for the entire nation" and Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal noted the mission underscored the "iron brotherhood" between the two countries.

    "This mission is not a finish line; I hope the next chapter of China-Pakistan space cooperation will grow from one astronaut and one flight to multiple joint flights, to the Moon, to Mars, and beyond," mentioned Ali.

    "Together with my Chinese crew mates, I will show that this friendship is real, not only on paper, but also in orbit.".

    In a recent development, ali will not be the first Pakistani in space, with Monaco-based polar explorer Namira Salim having flown on Virgin Galactic's Galactic 04 mission in October 2023. But he will be the first foreign astronaut to join a Chinese mission.

    During a short orbital flight expected to last around five days, Ali will carry out a series of experiments in the fields of biotechnology and photosynthetic microorganisms before returning to Earth aboard the Shenzhou-23 spacecraft, which docked at the Tiangong in May.

    China has poured billions of dollars into its space program. Its prized Tiangong space station is stewarded by teams of three astronauts that are typically rotated every six months.

    Beijing is aiming to land Chinese astronauts on the moon for the first time by 2030 and is seen as the main space rival to the United States, which is hoping to return to the lunar surface in 2028.

    #161818. Breaking: ‘GTA 6’ Is a Birder’s Paradise

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1373 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 WIRED ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: ‘GTA 6’ Is a Birder’s Paradise

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1373 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Grand Theft Auto VI has received near-universal acclaim and could be the highest-grossing entertainment launch in history.
    • Rockstar Games has filled the latest GTA installation with over 170 animal species that players can tally in their logbook.
    • Sources indicate that I myself am not a gamer, but I’m an avid birder based in Upcoming York City who’s familiar with a few indie birdwatching games like Alba and Flock Around, and I have done a bit of birding in Florida—which GTA VI is modeled after, with Vice City being a stand-in for Miami.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Grand Theft Auto VI has received near-universal acclaim and could be the highest-grossing entertainment launch in history. But it holds a more esoteric honor: It might be the most accurately rendered depiction of Florida’s bird life to appear in a video game.

    Rockstar Games has filled the latest GTA installation with over 170 animal species that players can tally in their logbook. At the same time, there’s been an explosion of interest in birdwatching, especially among young people, since the last GTA came out 13 years ago. While many players have gotten busy stealing jets and going to strip clubs, birders and streamers are doing “ornithologist runs” to see as many bird species as they can.

    Sources indicate that I myself am not a gamer, but I’m an avid birder based in Upcoming York City who’s familiar with a few indie birdwatching games like Alba and Flock Around, and I have done a bit of birding in Florida—which GTA VI is modeled after, with Vice City being a stand-in for Miami. So I was hungry to get my hands on GTA VI and see the birds for myself. Were the details of GTA VI’s avian NPCs as lifelike as its human ones? (Full disclosure that a friend of mine worked on the game, though not the birds specifically.).

    You receive a pair of binoculars with the first mission, and most of the map is open to explore once the intro is over, so you can begin your birding adventures immediately. I left the house and walked around town, trying to get a sense of the neighborhood and searching for places I knew I’d find wildlife, as I would in real life. It turns out you don’t have to look hard. Birds are everywhere in GTA VI—brown pelicans soared overhead, a flock of house sparrows alighted onto a telephone wire, and a blue jay stared down at me as I rounded a corner.

    I zeroed in on a gull perched atop a building and noticed its partial black hood of feathers, an adult laughing gull. In a sign of how committed Rockstar is to accurately portraying the real world, I walked further and noticed a bird with the same shape, but it was grayer and light on the black feathers, an immature laughing gull.

    This is GTA VI, and all means of improving your birding experience are at your disposal—legal or not. With that in mind, I headed toward the water and performed my first act of theft, jacking a kayak so I could inspect the mangroves and sandy islands in the bay. While motorboats were available, I opted for human-powered to avoid scaring the birds.

    The sky was filled with iconic South Florida birds like white ibises, magnificent frigate birds, and osprey. I shouted excitedly on spotting a flock of Caspian terns loafing on a small islet’s shore, then eyed a spotted sandpiper. The latter didn’t have its real-world analogue’s “twerking” strut (a substantial missed opportunity for a GTA game), but its physical appearance was accurate. I beached my kayak and went ashore, where I eyed a pair of great blue herons and then scared a tricolored heron from a shrub as I sprinted away from a crocodile I nearly stepped on.

    I was impressed by the game developer’s commitment to accurately rendering South Florida’s coastal mangrove habitats, which provide shelter for an abundance of fish, food for birds, and serve as a habitat for the threatened American crocodile. However, they only host so much avian diversity.

    According to recent reports, to see more species, I drove north through the various habitats in and around the fictional city of Leonida and stopped to scan the skies. I spotted American robins, northern mockingbirds, and “Latest World orioles,” the game’s analog to the Baltimore oriole, which I assumed is named as such because Baltimore is not part of the Grand Theft Auto universe. Downtown Vice City featured non-native peacocks and rock pigeons—the latter of which were introduced to North America in the 1600s. When I arrived at the pine-covered areas north of the city, I began seeing red-cockaded woodpeckers and scrub jays, an analog to the rare Florida scrub-jay that similarly inhabits sand pine areas north of Miami and is endemic to the state of Florida.

    According to recent reports, birders who’ve been to Florida will find Leonida’s abundance and distribution of wildlife familiar. As in meatspace, pelicans and ibises are constantly flying overhead, and wading birds fill every body of water. Birds are properly segregated into their habitats, with songbirds and city birds in built-up areas, shorebirds and long-legged wading birds in wetlands. In both the game and real life, despite intensive human development, birds still attempt to survive where they can.

    Sources indicate that the birds’ behaviors are also accurate beyond standing and flying. As I was trying to study my first bald eagle, a pair of crows flew over to chase it, a behavior regularly seen in the wild to scare large raptors away. Monk parakeets preened while perching on a wire, and a juvenile northern mockingbird did its characteristic wing flicking. Meanwhile, GTA VI’s great blue herons always seem to be having sex, not something I’ve noticed in real life but a silly detail nonetheless.

    Frankly, the whole experience of driving around while distractedly watching telephone wires and roadsides or pulling over to check every little water body is itself the most accurate representation of the Florida birding experience.

    My other birding friends who have played the game concurred. “The first thing I thought was how closely this resembles birding in Florida,” says accomplished bird author Nick Lund, who has done extensive birdwatching in Red Dead Redemption II, another game where avian life is a significant part of gameplay, and is right now doing a GTA VI birding speed run. He’s noticed other in-game birding Easter eggs—for example, he’s encountered spot-breasted orioles, a Central American species introduced to southeastern Florida that birdwatchers specifically target when visiting Miami.

    It has been revealed that while impressive in its fidelity to real life, GTA VI’s avian depictions aren’t 100 percent accurate. I found the flight styles and silhouettes of many birds to be a little off, while some renditions missed the mark—the abundant crows all feel too long and pale. While walking around Jason’s neighborhood, Lund and I both noticed the apparent song of the bananaquit, a Caribbean species that rarely appears in the US. The game is also filled with whooping cranes, one of the rarest birds in the US. They’re also mostly gone from Florida after an unsuccessful reintroduction effort, where sandhill cranes are much more common. (Maybe the makers of GTA VI are telling real-world conservationists to try harder next time.) Lund flagged that the roseate spoonbill seems to make the call of the willow ptarmigan—a detail he also noticed in RDR II. And somehow I’ve yet to spot a bird in a tree, but this may be a skill problem.

    Ultimately, GTA VI isn’t a birdwatching game, and does lag behind the real world and birdwatching-specific games in terms of avian content. Sixty-two species might sound like a lot, but birders in Miami-Dade County have spotted more than 240 species in November 2026 alone, and one real-life birder in Miami spotted 61 species in a two-hour stint on the day of the game’s release.

    In a recent development, there’s a certain magic and unpredictability to birdwatching that the game doesn’t nail—finding a migratory warbler in a hotel parking lot, catching an egret hunting anoles in a topiary, or spotting an out-of-place vagrant bird are all real-life thrills the game can’t fully capture. Of course, GTA VI also has an actual plot and storyline that I surmise might be slightly more notable to its developers and the majority of the gaming public than solely building the world’s most accurate Florida birding simulator.

    According to recent reports, still, GTA VI’s animal observation mechanics have continued to delight after 12 hours of play. Birding is certainly an auxiliary part of the game, rather than its core thrust—but if you’re a birder wondering whether to play the game just for its birds, I think you’ll still have plenty of fun.

    Breaking: GTA 6 player gets social ban on PSN after sending a photo of in-game nudity

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (483 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Engadget

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Apparently just because it’s in the game doesn’t mean sharing “obscene” content is okay.
    • Sources indicate that grand Theft Auto 6 has dominated everyone's attention since it came out last week and broke the record for the most day one retail sales in entertainment history.
    • In a recent development, according to X user @derrickgott007, they received a notice from PlayStation Safety saying their account was being temporarily suspended from using social features for 30 days after breaching the company's code of conduct regarding pornographic or obscene content.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Apparently just because it’s in the game doesn’t mean sharing “obscene” content is okay.

    Sources indicate that grand Theft Auto 6 has dominated everyone's attention since it came out last week and broke the record for the most day one retail sales in entertainment history. Unfortunately, not everyone's experience has been 100 percent positive, especially now that one player has been hit with a social ban on PSN after sharing a photo of naked people taken with the game's built-in camera feature.

    In a recent development, according to X user @derrickgott007, they received a notice from PlayStation Safety saying their account was being temporarily suspended from using social features for 30 days after breaching the company's code of conduct regarding pornographic or obscene content. The glitch is that the user claims the offending image was actually a photo taken using GTA 6's camera feature of a nudist resort they found inside the game before sharing it with someone else on PSN.

    Sources indicate that in this case, if you simply go by what's outlined in PlayStation's code of conduct, technically this player did break the rules as there's a specific bullet point about not sharing, soliciting, accessing, distributing or storing "material that is obscene, pornographic, or illegal." However, where things get a bit murky is that the source of the offending material came from a game being played on a PS5 that is also sold digitally by Sony itself. This feels a bit hypocritical as it seems that it's okay for a game to contain nudity or pornographic material, but as soon as you take a photo or screenshot of noted content, suddenly you're in violation of PlayStation's guidelines.

    Furthermore, while a social ban might not sound that bad as the user will still have access to some games, because online multiplayer falls under the umbrella of social activity, @derrickgott007 says they can't even play Call of Duty during their 30-day suspension.

    Another interesting topic that incidents like this bring up is how often regular people agree to things they haven't fully read or acknowledged due to a manufacturer's terms of service (ToS) or end-user license agreement (EULA). Often, these documents are so long and onerous that people blindly skip past them and hit the checkbox just so they can use the thing they paid for. Some organizations like the ToS;DR project have made efforts to call out companies with terms of services that are unnecessarily dense or difficult to understand, but it remains an ongoing glitch for almost everyone in modern society.

    Sadly, even though PlayStation's guidelines seem a bit contradictory, this incident should serve as a public service announcement to anyone considering taking a photo or screenshot of potentially obscene material in GTA 6 (or other games) with their PS5, as they need to be extra careful or else they risk getting hit with a similar ban.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, rumors have been swirling for days that we would be getting a final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday, the penultimate film in the Marvel Cinematic Universe’s Phase Six, heralding the end of the so-called “Multiverse Saga.” The rumors were true: Marvel just released the trailer, featuring pretty much every superhero ever represented in the MCU. And it looks like the Avengers will face consequences for messing with the timeline to reverse the blip in Endgame.

    Recent findings suggest that as previously reported, the film takes place 14 months after the events of Thunderbolts*. Per the official logline: “Beloved heroes from three distinct universes will be set on a deadly collision course and face an existential threat unlike anything they’ve ever encountered.” Those universes are Earth-616 (the Avengers, Wakandans, and Upcoming Avengers), Earth-828 (Fantastic Four), and the “original” X-Men.

    Cast-wise, we have Avengers favorites Thor (Chris Hemsworth), the new Captain America (Anthony Mackie), Bucky Barnes (Sebastian Stan), Ant-Man (Paul Rudd), Falcon (Danny Ramirez), and Loki (Tom Hiddleston). Then there’s the Wakandan contingent: Shuri as the new Black Panther (Letitia Wright), M’Baku (Winston Duke), and Namor (Tenoch Huerta Mejia), as well as Alex Livinalli as Namor’s ally, Attuma. And, of course, Robert Downey Jr. as Doctor Doom.

    We also have the Thunderbolts* (aka Upcoming Avengers): John Walker/US Agent (Wyatt Russell), Yelena Belova (Florence Pugh), Bob/Sentry (Lewis Pullman), Red Guardian (David Harbour), and Ghost (Hannah John-Kamen). And the Fantastic Four: Reed Richards (Pedro Pascal), Sue Storm (Vanessa Kirby), Ben Grimm (Ebon Moss-Bachrach), and Johnny Storm (Joseph Quinn). We’ll also see Charles Xavier (Patrick Stewart), Beast (Kelsey Grammer), Magneto (Ian McKellen), Mystique (Rebecca Romijn), Nightcrawler (Alan Cumming), and Cyclops (James Marsden).

    It has been revealed that for good measure, Marvel threw in Gambit (Channing Tatum) and Xu Shang-Chi (Simu Liu). There will be plenty of cameos, like Steve Rogers (Chris Evans), revealed in one of four sneak teasers last year. We can also expect to see (at least briefly) Peggy Carter (Hayley Atwell), Spider-Man (Tom Holland), Hawkeye (Jeremy Renner), Doctor Strange (Benedict Cumberbatch), Thor’s adopted daughter, Love (India Rose Hemsworth), and Scott Lang’s daughter, Cassie (Kathryn Newton).

    According to recent reports, the first trailer dropped in July, just before San Diego Comic-Con, and it just consisted of a heck of a lot of cameos, as the superheroes from the three universes met each other over an ominous voiceover by Thor, warning of an unprecedented threat. It ended with the return of Steve Rogers—and guess what, he’s still worthy of Thor’s hammer, Mjölnir. The following month, Marvel dropped another trailer during its D23 fan event, hinting at Doctor Doom’s tragic backstory.

    Sources indicate that rogers features prominently in the fresh trailer, which opens with him and Peggy discussing how they made the right choice, but Steve still feels bad about hiding this truth from their son, who is now a young teen. We knew he had opted to stay in the past and build a life with Peggy at the end of Endgame; what we didn’t know is that they did this in the same alternate universe as the Fantastic Four, who show up to recruit him to the latest cause.

    Recent findings suggest that “Years ago, we did what was needed to make the world right,” Rogers continues in a voiceover. “But we didn’t know those choices would have consequences.” Whatever the roots of Doom’s grudge against the Avengers, he believes “all of you have lived stolen lives,” adding an ominous: “But now you must give them back.”.

    The rest is largely footage we’ve seen before, with Thor admitting, “I don’t even know who half of you are” to the assembled superheroes, before making his call for them to “stand together” against Doom. Among the latest footage is Marsden’s Cyclops facing off against Doom and several Sentinels: He calls, “To me, my X-Men,” except it’s everyone who responds. We also see Steve and Thor bantering about how Steve wielding Mjölnir bothers the Norse god more than he cares to admit. There’s no sign of Wanda Maximoff/The Scarlet Witch, whom Doom revived in a post-credits scene at the end of VisionQuest. She might be among the trio of Latverian witches that briefly appear in the trailer.

    Verdict: We don’t know if Doomsday will measure up to Infinity War and End Game, but it’s bound to provide a spectacle.

    In a recent development, avengers: Doomsday hits theaters on December 18, 2026. It will battle it out against Dune: Part III, which also releases that same day. Avengers: Secret Wars is at the moment slated for release on December 17, 2027, and will mark the conclusion of the MCU’s Phase Six.

    We've also got further confirmation the iPhone Air 2 will have a second camera.

    According to recent reports, apple seems to have adopted a new strategy for the iPhone launch, splitting it into two phases. After launching the premium iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo in September, Apple is preparing new versions of the lower-priced models — and it looks like they'll look a lot more like the more expensive iPhones. CAD images of the new iPhone 18e seen by Engadget show a redesigned camera bump on the back of the phone, similar to the one on the Pro models. The images come from a source familiar with Apple's supply chain who who had previously shared accurate tips on the colors of the iPhone 17 and iPhone 18 Pro before they were confirmed.

    The current iPhone 17e doesn't have a camera bump — instead, the lens has a small protrusion and sits flush against the back of the phone, with the microphone and LED flash also embedded in cutouts directly in the rear glass. But according to CAD images seen by Engadget, Apple appears to be considering changing that with the iPhone 18e. The renders show an almost square camera bump measuring about 28 mm by 35 mm that houses the single rear camera, the LED flash and the rear microphone. It's somewhat similar to the camera module on the M5 iPad Pro (which you can see in the image below).

    Interestingly, it seems that the iPhone 18e will be the only model to feature this upcoming camera plateau. The same files include the CADs for the base iPhone 18 and the iPhone Air 2, both of which are expected to launch alongside the 18e next spring. The base iPhone 18 will keep the exact same design, but now with a thicker camera module — increasing from 3.45mm (0.14 inches) to 3.8mm (0.15 inches). Apple has been using the same 48-megapixel Sony IMX904 sensor for its base models since the iPhone 15, so a thicker camera module could mean new sensors or upgraded cameras.

    In a recent development, as for the iPhone Air 2, the CADs seen by Engadget corroborate previous rumors that Apple's ultra-thin phone will feature a second rear camera — not a surprise given that its single lens was one of the main complaints about it. Although the Air 2 will remain 5.6mm thick, the camera module will increase in thickness from 3.45mm (0.14 inches) to 3.8mm (0.15 inches), with the two lenses aligned horizontally. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, the leaker Digital Chat Station and analyst Jeff Pu have all said Apple is adding an ultra-wide lens to the second-generation Air, and the CAD images back those reports up.

    In a recent development, also, the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 are expected to keep the same Dynamic Island as current models rather than the smaller cutout on the iPhone 18 Pro. Of course, these changes may end up being scrapped and never see the light of day, since Apple still has some time before they hit the stores next year.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that when Notable Capital poured roughly 10% of the U.S.
    • But investors at Notable, formerly known as GGV Capital before its 2024 split from its China operations, were confident in Anthropic’s future.
    • “We just knew that for AI, the developer is at the center because they’re the early adopters,” Tung, a co-founder of the firm, told TechCrunch.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that when Notable Capital poured roughly 10% of the U.S. portion of its $1 billion-plus fund into Anthropic’s Series E, many limited partners were perplexed by the massive bet. Claude’s maker was still trailing its biggest rival, OpenAI, and DeepSeek had released its R1 model just weeks earlier, threatening to overtake closed-source competitors. Moreover, at $61.5 billion, Anthropic’s valuation was by far the highest that the predominantly early-stage venture firm had invested at in its 25-year history.

    But investors at Notable, formerly known as GGV Capital before its 2024 split from its China operations, were confident in Anthropic’s future. A team that included managing partners Hans Tung and Glenn Solomon and principal Dan Cahana crunched the numbers and found that developers were increasingly favoring Claude over ChatGPT, using Claude 70% of the time, a reversal from the previous year.

    “We just knew that for AI, the developer is at the center because they’re the early adopters,” Tung, a co-founder of the firm, told TechCrunch.

    Having navigated the complexities of U.S.-China relations firsthand, Notable was also convinced that “mission-critical” work would always require U.S.-based, closed-source models, Tung mentioned.

    Industry observers note that less than two years later, Notable’s LPs are no longer questioning the outsized investment. On Wednesday, Anthropic raised $81.3 billion in the largest IPO in history, reaching a fully diluted valuation of about $1.5 trillion before its shares began trading the next day, a paper return of roughly 15 times.

    It has been revealed that notable is, of course, not the only firm sitting on a massive paper windfall from Anthropic. Even traditional late-stage investors, who rarely see venture-scale multiples, are set for a substantial win.

    In a recent development, singaporean sovereign wealth fund GIC had been researching Anthropic throughout 2024, but it didn’t make its first investment until after Chris Emanuel, head of the fund’s tech investments, met with Anthropic CFO Krishna Rao at Che Fico, an Italian restaurant in San Francisco, in early 2025. Rao helped pique Emanuel’s interest in the tech giant by showing that model improvements were driving rising enterprise adoption. GIC then made its first investment in Anthropic’s Series F, a round declared in September 2025 at a $183 billion valuation.

    Sources indicate that “Claude Code was just released then,” Emanuel told TechCrunch. “It was very early, but even then, we could see signs that it was really popular with developers.” GIC’s conviction in the AI lab was so high that the fund later led Anthropic’s Series G alongside Coatue at a $380 billion valuation, and returned as one of the co-leads for the pre-IPO round at $965 billion. Across the three rounds, GIC invested more than $4.5 billion in Anthropic, amassing a stake equal to about 1% of the company after its IPO, according to a person familiar with GIC’s financials.

    Lillian Li, who leads U.S. growth investments at Baillie Gifford, began studying Anthropic and speaking with its team nearly two years before first investing in the firm’s Series F. Baillie Gifford invested in the Claude maker once it became clear that the company was “executing consistently” on its vision while generating strong revenue and “compelling gross margins,” Li told TechCrunch.

    After Baillie Gifford’s initial investment, Anthropic continued to deliver on its promises, expanding into industries such as legal services and life sciences, as well as broader applications like Cowork and cybersecurity, Li noted.

    In a recent development, “It’s actually quite incredible how consistent they have been with how quickly everything’s been changing,” she added. Baillie Gifford went on to invest a total of $1.5 billion across three funding rounds, a bet that has generated substantial paper gains for the investment manager, as well as for dozens of other backers who invested at what once seemed like astronomical valuations.

    • A large-scale search operation for a suspected lion sighted in woodland north of Istanbul has ended, with the animal in question found to be neither a lion nor any other type of big cat, according to the Istanbul governor's office.
    • The governor's office first issued a statement on Sunday evening saying that security cameras had captured footage of a lion on the loose in Sariyer, north of Istanbul's European side.
    • The parks authority also said in an online statement that police officers in the area had spotted "an animal resembling a lion" on surveillance cameras.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A large-scale search operation for a suspected lion sighted in woodland north of Istanbul has ended, with the animal in question found to be neither a lion nor any other type of big cat, according to the Istanbul governor's office.

    The governor's office first issued a statement on Sunday evening saying that security cameras had captured footage of a lion on the loose in Sariyer, north of Istanbul's European side. It said "the lion has been located and the efforts to capture it were underway.".

    The parks authority also said in an online statement that police officers in the area had spotted "an animal resembling a lion" on surveillance cameras.

    Turkish media published grainy images purportedly showing a lioness walking through a grassy area. Some media reports suggested it had escaped from a nearby home.

    The Istanbul Chief Public Prosecutor's Office also issued a statement saying it had launched an investigation focused on identifying the lion's owner.

    After a day of searching, however, the Istanbul governor's office noted "no ​concrete evidence indicating ‌the presence of a lion was found.".

    It said ⁠based on fresh footage, "it has been determined ⁠that the ​animal in the footage is neither a lion nor any other species of major cat.".

    The governor's office did not provide further information about what the animal seen in the footage was.

    The earlier reports about a lion on the loose had sparked an outrage among activists.

    Northern Forests Defense, an independent ecology advocacy movement, called for "the individuals who illegally held this lion captive to be identified and brought to justice.".

    "Removing wild animals from their natural habitats and keeping them in captivity in villas is a crime," the organization stated on X.

    Wildlife conservationist Gokce Coskun said on X that "there are thousands of people keeping lions illegally in Turkey" and "licensed 'lion parks' have sprung up everywhere.".

    Last year, a lion that escaped from a "theme park" near the southern city of Antalya was shot dead after attacking a man.

    Doganay Tolunay, an ecology professor at Istanbul University, noted questions must be asked about how a globally threatened species was brought into Turkey, how it passed through customs and why those keeping it have not been identified.

    Although keeping wild animals as pets is forbidden in Turkey, the country has become a hub for the illegal wild animal trade as traffickers exploit its air links to Africa and Asia.

    In December 2024, a young gorilla was rescued after being discovered in a crate at Istanbul Airport.

    It has been revealed that this year, Black Friday falls on Nov. 27. While retailers often start featuring their best markdowns on Black Friday itself, there are plenty of early deals worth shopping in the lead-up. Most retailers' official sales do start well before the big day, so shopping strategically ahead of time can save you from missing out on a deal entirely (or dealing with the chaos the day after Thanksgiving).

    Industry observers note that cyber Monday takes place on the Monday following Thanksgiving. This year, the shopping event takes place on Monday, Nov. 30. While Cyber Monday originally began as an online counterpart to in-person shopping on Black Friday, the two events have merged into an extended online shopping bonanza.

    It has been revealed that the mega-retailer just wrapped up its October Prime Day sale, and naturally, it's also getting in on the Black Friday action. For 2026, Amazon's official Black Friday sales kicked off on Nov. 19, which means deals are already live. Amazon has an incentive to spread out the shopping (to give its delivery drivers a break), so you no longer have to wait until Thanksgiving to save. Deals will continue to go live through Nov. 30.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Uber is piloting a latest feature in the U.S.
    • The option, which uses the front camera of the Uber driver’s phone to record the entire drive, will show up as “Recorded Rides” in the app.
    • The ride-hailing organization is starting the pilot in Baltimore, Raleigh, Indianapolis, and St.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Uber is piloting a latest feature in the U.S. that offers rides in which drivers have enabled the company’s recording feature, Record My Ride.

    The option, which uses the front camera of the Uber driver’s phone to record the entire drive, will show up as “Recorded Rides” in the app.

    The ride-hailing organization is starting the pilot in Baltimore, Raleigh, Indianapolis, and St. Louis and will expand to more locations later.

    Industry observers note that uber said it is testing recorded rides specifically for rides booked at late night or those involving teens. Earlier this year, it introduced a live video streaming feature for rides booked for teenagers. In another test, the firm had enabled audio recording for late-night trips in some cities.

    The company is also testing a feature that will turn on recording when the app detects the ride going off-course, or when the vehicle might have had an accident.

    The company mentioned drivers can opt out of recording through the Settings panel. Similarly, riders can also decline permission to record their rides via an in-app notification.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, ben McKenzie promised his wife that he was through with being an activist; that he’d go back to the acting gigs that had made him famous. At the end of his documentary taking on the cryptocurrency industry, Everyone Is Lying to You for Money,” the former star of The O.C. and Gotham turned to his spouse and fellow actor Morena Baccarin and swore he was done.

    Turns out, that scene might need an edit. McKenzie is launching a latest nonprofit, The Public Trust and Transparency Project, that not only continues his battle with the crypto business but widens it to fight prediction markets like Polymarket and Kalshi.

    McKenzie tells WIRED he’s worried about “the gamification of the economy and the notion that we're turning everything into gambling—both investments, in the form of cryptocurrencies, and “prediction markets,” which look an awful lot like online casinos.”.

    It has been revealed that “The more gambling gets into our culture, the more people feel like it's somehow a good idea to view these things as legitimate investment strategies,” he notes. The prediction markets reject the comparison (although 80 percent of Kalshi’s trades came from sports in September, according to Bloomberg). McKenzie rejects the rejection: “I mean, if your investment strategy is, ‘I'm going to gamble on the Spurs-Knicks,’ like, come on! So there's a real, real problem here.”.

    John Reed Stark, who spent 18 years in the Securities and Exchange Commission’s enforcement division, will serve as an adviser to the Project. American Kleptocracy author Casey Michel and Tonazin Carmona, who runs economic policy for the left-of-center Century Foundation, will sit on the board.

    It has been revealed that the group is coming together at a time when regulators and law enforcement officials at every level are looking to rein in prediction markets. Federal regulators have introduced latest probes into both major prediction markets. The GOP-led House Oversight Committee recently released its investigation into US troops and government insiders trading on insider knowledge on Polymarket and Kalshi. The Senate just passed a bill prohibiting prediction markets for military operations and assassinations. Executives at the markets know they’re in for a rough few months; Kalshi even launched an ad campaign, starring Martha Stewart, reminding its people not to trade on confidential information.

    According to recent reports, but insider trading is only one concern among many. There’s also the problem you find in old-school gambling houses too: The vast majority of people who use the markets lose their money. A recent Wall Street Journal report shows that .01 percent of accounts take in two-thirds of all of the profits on Polymarket. On Kalshi, unprofitable accounts outpace profitable ones by almost three to one.

    Sources indicate that then there’s the corruption angle, which McKenzie claims is going to be front-and-center for the Project, especially with it featuring as a top matter in the recent midterm elections. Donald Trump Jr. was, until recently, a paid adviser to Kalshi. Trump Jr.’s venture firm, 1789 Capital, made its latest and biggest in a series of investments in Polymarket over the summer; months earlier, the Trump Justice Department sued the state of Minnesota when it tried to ban the prediction markets in the state. (At a recent conference, Polymarket CEO Shayne Coplan called Trump Jr.’s involvement “heavily overblown. We have all types of investors.”).

    In a recent development, prediction markets have been around for hundreds of years, as a forthcoming book on the subject notes. American academics have been turning to them as teaching tools since the late ’80s. Their advocates note that they can be an effective way to hedge against risk, and a form of trading on sports that’s far more consumer-friendly than the online gambling houses. “I accept that there may be some utility,” McKenzie notes. “I'm not saying these things should not exist. I'm just saying they need to be properly regulated.”.

    McKenzie’s initiative will be to push Congress in that direction, sort of the inverse of how the former actor lobbied publicly and privately against the “Clarity Act,” which would’ve brought cryptocurrencies into the financial mainstream. (The bill was rejected in September.).

    That pressure is only bound to increase when Democrats take control of Congress next year. “In the bold new world starting [on the] first Monday in January,” Representative Frank Lucas, an Oklahoma Republican, told Politico, “nobody’s untouchable anymore.”.

    Your older, discontinued AirTags can still serve a purpose

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Before you toss your original AirTag, here are a few ways to keep it useful.
    • We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
    • Earlier this year, Apple introduced the first new generation AirTag since the original debuted in 2021.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Before you toss your original AirTag, here are a few ways to keep it useful.

    We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

    Earlier this year, Apple introduced the first new generation AirTag since the original debuted in 2021. And while you might still be able to find first-generation Apple AirTags for purchase on some websites, Apple doesn't sell them anymore. The manufacturer is now focusing solely on the new model and leaving the original AirTag behind. But the old ones are still supported in the Find My app, so there's lots of ways you can continue to use them.

    The newer Apple AirTag offers an expanded finding range thanks to the second-generation ultrawideband chip, upgraded Bluetooth chip, improved Precision Finding from up to 50 percent farther away and a louder speaker. Given how cheap Apple AirTags are ($29 on Amazon) and all the upgrades with the second-gen model, you'll probably want to grab a few for your most precious items.

    But that doesn't mean you should toss your old AirTags. They can be relocated to secondary items, kept as backups for your most key gear or handed down to friends and family.

    An AirTag that still works is worth hanging onto. Use newer AirTags for your keys, purse, wallet, child's backpack and maybe even pet collar and move your old AirTags to secondary items. Toss one in your glove compartment or trunk of your car in case of theft or to keep track of your newly licensed teen if they turn off location sharing in Find My. Or put one in your luggage as a secondary method of tracking its location if it's lost or misplaced.

    According to recent reports, keep one in your child's jacket pocket so they're still trackable if they don't have their backpack (some parents even stitch them into their kids' shoes). Clip one secondary set of keys you often misplace in the house, like the key to the back door or home office filing cabinet. While the range is farther and the speaker louder on the upcoming AirTag, both are still sufficient on the older model for finding items within the home. My son used Precision Finding with an old AirTag the other day to locate his house keys and it worked perfectly well.

    You could also get creative and affix one to the inside of your headphones case or toss one in your dressy purse, clutch or wallet so you don't have to move the upcoming AirTag back and forth when you switch. Or keep one with items that are tough to find in a cluttered space, like holiday decorations in the attic, a toolbox in the garage or a small remote in the game room. AirTags use easily replaceable CR2032 batteries that last about a year with normal usage and under normal conditions.

    Since the new Precision Finding benefits of the second-generation Apple AirTag are only supported with iPhone 15 and newer models, you won't be able to use one if you have an older phone. In this case, it's still worthwhile to continue using a first-gen Apple AirTag until you upgrade your phone. Standard Precision Finding works with iPhone 11 through 14 models, so consider handing over the old AirTag to a friend or family member with an older iPhone, like a parent or grandparent. They can use it for their wallet, purse, eyeglasses case or other item they often misplace.

    It has been revealed that if you want to be extra diligent, use a second older AirTag with a new battery as a backup in case the battery in your new AirTag dies before you get the chance to replace it. A second AirTag can also add security. Think putting the new AirTag under your bicycle seat and the older one under the bike's bottle cage or inside the bell. A thief might find one and dispose of it, but likely won't find both.

    Recent findings suggest that some buyback sites in certain countries also purchase old AirTags. While Apple doesn't accept AirTags for trade-in, sites like Sell Techs in the UK and BuyBackWorld do. So you could make a bit of cash by selling them. Just because older AirTags are slowly becoming obsolete, that doesn't mean they don't still have their use.

    The decision marks an extraordinary comeback for one of the tech industry’s most influential executives, whose abrupt departure raised questions about national security and the future of the world’s most valuable chipmaker. Notably, the U.S. government itself played a role in his return: Nvidia’s board remarked it consulted senior government officials before determining that Huang posed no national security risk.

Trump said in a post on Truth Social that the board “made the correct and proper decision to return” Huang to the position, noting that the U.S. government has no reason to believe that Nvidia poses any risk to national security.

    Trump also noted the U.S. attorney general confirmed that the U.S. government doesn’t have any evidence that Huang engaged in any illegal activity.

    A long list of high-profile tech executives were pushing the board — in social media posts and publicly aired interviews — to bring Huang back, including SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, Atoms founder Travis Kalanick, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan — all of whom signed a petition pushing for reinstatement.

    Sources indicate that the tech giant said the board’s unanimous decision followed a series of discussions and meetings with Huang, after which they were “satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia.”.

Jones remarked they didn’t intend to reinstate Huang. Nvidia had even retained executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles to find a permanent replacement.

    According to recent reports, jones, along with the rest of the board, now has a different view. In a prepared statement, Jones noted the board believes Huang is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of its stockholders, employees, partners, and customers.

    According to recent reports, “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the company,” Jones said. “We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as Nvidia’s Chief Financial Officer.”.

    In a statement, Huang remarked he was honored to return to his role as the head of the company he co-founded in 1993.

    In a recent development, “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Huang stated. “I want to thank the Nvidia Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading Nvidia during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”.

    Reports: Russia may launch nuclear weapon into orbit as soon as next month

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (908 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Western intelligence officials worry that Russia could launch a nuclear-armed satellite into orbit before the end of the year, suggesting the country’s development of a satellite-killing weapon of mass destruction is more advanced than previously thought, German media reported Monday.
    • It has been revealed that the orbiting nuclear weapon would threaten thousands of satellites in low-Earth orbit, including military and commercial communications networks like Starshield and Starlink.
    • Sources indicate that US lawmakers briefed on government intelligence first disclosed Russia’s ambition to deploy a space-based nuclear weapon in early 2024.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Western intelligence officials worry that Russia could launch a nuclear-armed satellite into orbit before the end of the year, suggesting the country’s development of a satellite-killing weapon of mass destruction is more advanced than previously thought, German media reported Monday.

    It has been revealed that the orbiting nuclear weapon would threaten thousands of satellites in low-Earth orbit, including military and commercial communications networks like Starshield and Starlink. A nuclear-armed satellite would also put at risk Western military surveillance satellites and human spaceflight platforms like the International Space Station. A nuclear detonation in orbit would be indiscriminate, also knocking out Russia’s own spacecraft and Chinese satellites.

    Sources indicate that US lawmakers briefed on government intelligence first disclosed Russia’s ambition to deploy a space-based nuclear weapon in early 2024. At the time, US officials noted Russia had launched a test satellite in 2022 to test the effects of radiation on space hardware and pave the way for a future nuclear-armed craft, but that Russia had not yet sent a nuclear weapon into orbit.

    Reporting from three German news outlets—public broadcasters NDR and WDR and the Munich-based newspaper Süddeutsche Zeitung—indicates Russia’s launch of a nuclear-armed satellite could be imminent. The report claims Western intelligence agencies, including the German Armed Forces and Federal Intelligence Service, believe Russia is preparing to deploy the weapon in space this year. Several NATO countries have exchanged their findings on the matter.

    Sources indicate that the nuclear-armed satellite, designated Sputnik-S, has been in storage in the greater Moscow area for years, the German news report stated. German Space Command believes the satellite could be rolled out as early as December. Once in orbit, a nuclear weapon could loiter for months or years, ready for detonation on the command of Russian military forces.

    In a recent development, the Kremlin dismissed the report. “Given the number of qualifiers like ‘allegedly’ and ‘possibly’—not to mention the fact that the claims are attributed to some unspecified source—they are hardly worth taking seriously,” said Dmitry Peskov, spokesperson for Russian President Vladimir Putin.

    If it goes ahead, the launch would violate the 1967 Outer Space Treaty, which prohibits the deployment of weapons of mass destruction in space. Russia is a party to the treaty, but the Russian government vetoed a draft UN Security Council resolution in 2024 seeking to reaffirm the prohibition on weapons of mass destruction in space.

    German Chancellor Friedrich Merz did not address the timing of the potential launch when asked about it at a press conference Monday.

    “The news that Russia is planning to arm space with nuclear weapons is not upcoming, but that doesn’t make it any less shocking,” Merz stated. “It reveals the extent to which Russia is apparently prepared to escalate the situation.”.

    The German news reports published Monday come a month after the US military’s Defense Intelligence Agency highlighted the threat of a Russian nuclear-armed satellite.

    According to recent reports, “Russia is developing a satellite designed to carry a nuclear weapon despite its obligation to comply with the 1967 Outer Space Treaty,” the DIA stated in a public report on challenges to security in space. “A space-based capability such as this could cause rapid and sudden loss or degradation of thousands of satellites operated by countries and companies around the world, as well as to the vital communications, navigation, scientific, meteorological, commercial, and national security services they provide.

    “Beyond its immediate effects, a nuclear detonation in space would also leave lingering radiation belts, which could persist for years and damage satellites that initially were only temporarily disrupted,” the DIA mentioned.

    The Pentagon increasingly relies upon satellites to support military operations. US forces have used satellites for navigation, strategic communications, missile warning, and surveillance for decades. The US military is now launching satellites to support real-time targeting of missiles, aircraft, and land and sea vehicles, incorporating space platforms into a wider array of offensive and defensive operations.

    In September, the Pentagon confirmed the Space Force has placed unspecified weapons in orbit. There is no international ban on conventional weapons in space.

    Leaders in China, which has the second-highest number of operational satellites, have not made any public statements on Russia’s nuclear-armed satellite program. China would be most impacted by a nuclear detonation in orbit after the United States. Russia has comparatively fewer satellites in orbit, and its military spending in recent years has focused on fighting the war in Ukraine rather than modernizing its space program.

    If Russia does launch a nuclear-armed satellite, it would be an escalation of the country’s already-bellicose behavior in orbit. Russia has tested what US officials say is a kinetic anti-satellite weapon and is now operationalizing the system, according to a top US Space Force general. The weapon works by firing projectiles from one satellite toward another.

    Recent findings suggest that russia has also launched military satellites into orbits near the US government’s most sophisticated Keyhole-class spy satellites. Last month, a Russian satellite approached very near a commercial radar reconnaissance satellite owned by Finnish company ICEYE. The Russian spacecraft flew within “tens of meters” of the ICEYE satellite, which provides surveillance imagery to the Ukrainian military, before backing away, a US official stated.

    The kinds of weapons Russia has demonstrated so far would take out only a small number of satellites. A proliferated constellation like Starlink or the Pentagon’s upcoming airborne and ground targeting satellites could absorb such an attack. A nuclear detonation would threaten entire networks.

    #161789. Industry News: German directors' doc on stolen film wins International Emmy Award

    📅 24 Feb 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1044 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: German directors' doc on stolen film wins International Emmy Award

    📅 24 Feb 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1044 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, it sounds like the plot of a screenplay, but it happened to two Berlin film students in real life.
    • Moritz Henneberg and Julius Drost had created an animated short film for their final project at university.
    • "Butty" tells the tale of a household robot that gets kicked out when it can't do its job properly.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, it sounds like the plot of a screenplay, but it happened to two Berlin film students in real life. The documentary they made out of their unusual story, "The Talented Mr. F," has now won an International Emmy Award.

    Moritz Henneberg and Julius Drost had created an animated short film for their final project at university.

    "Butty" tells the tale of a household robot that gets kicked out when it can't do its job properly.

    Sources indicate that when the two filmmakers posted the work on YouTube, this touching tale rapidly went viral. After generating a huge amount of hits, the duo decided to submit their work to festivals — but they were in for a shock: Organizers told them the film had already been submitted under a different name.

    US student Samuel Felinton downloaded the film, made minimal edits, gave it a newly introduced title, "T-130," and removed the original credits. As the alleged author, he went on to win numerous prizes and made a name for himself in the United States.

    Shocked by the blatant theft of their work, Henneberg and Drost sought legal advice. They were told that if they opted to sue, the process would be arduous and costly. So, the filmmakers took matters into their own hands and went to the US to confront Felinton — filming their journey along the way.

    "We'd already made documentary films," Henneberg told DW. "And the idea just popped into our heads: This is a brilliant story — let's make a documentary about it.".

    The two directors had developed a kind of fascination for the man who'd stolen their film.

    "We looked at his vlogs and sort of took a deep dive into his world," remarked Drost. "We almost saw him as a kind of celebrity. We discovered a lot about him and really wanted to meet him in person.".

    Recent findings suggest that while family and friends reacted with anger, the two young filmmakers remained surprisingly calm. They were more perplexed than anything: "Our families and friends hated Samuel. But we just wanted to understand what had happened," they remarked.

    Sources indicate that the pair put together a film crew and traveled to Morgantown, West Virginia — the university town where Felinton lives. With the help of a Fresh York filmmaker pretending to make a documentary about young animators, they won Felinton's trust — and then Henneberg, Drost and Felinton were finally in a room together.

    The two German filmmakers had prepared for all manner of scenarios ahead of the meeting: "We expected an emotional reaction — that he'd run away, cry, be ashamed or get aggressive. But he remained completely calm. That was the only thing we hadn't bargained for. We thought his world would implode. But he demonstrated barely any emotion at all," they recalled.

    Felinton explained how he'd shortened and "improved" the film and that this was how it became such a success. He agreed to transfer any prize money. His manner was cool and matter-of-fact, which Drost and Henneberg found both unsettling and fascinating. After their chat, the three barbecued together and played a round of basketball.

    Industry observers note that later, many viewers accused the two German filmmakers of being too soft on the plagiarist. Others praised their approach.

    According to recent reports, "The reactions were very divided," said Drost. "Some said we should've sued him or punched him in the face. Others said we'd shown upcoming ways to resolve conflicts.".

    Industry observers note that "And in the end, it wasn't personal," added Henneberg. "He wanted to make something of himself — he could've taken another film. But if a significant studio like Pixar had stolen our film, that'd be quite a different story.".

    And so, Henneberg and Drost made the conscious decision to keep things respectful.

    They didn't want to "publicly embarrass him or punish him any more than necessary," they mentioned, adding that their documentary was sufficient "revenge.".

    The title of the documentary, "Der talentierte Mister F." ("The Talented Mister F."), is no coincidence. It's a play on the movie title "The Talented Mr. Ripley," the story of a young man who assumes the identity of a wealthy heir and ends up mired in a web of lies, fraud and, finally, murder. And just like Mr. Ripley, Felinton had also assumed a false identity.

    Felinton did actually end up sending them the trophies he had won, as well as a sum of money.

    In a recent development, for their part, however, the festivals preferred to keep their distance from the saga. As one organizer mentioned: The prize has been awarded, and there's nothing we can do about it — it's up to these guys to work things out between themselves.

    For the original filmmakers themselves, the scandal has also had a positive impact: Since the documentary was released in Germany in October 2025, their animation film has garnered even more attention on YouTube. Henneberg and Drost uploaded it again, and in the credits, special thanks also go out to Samuel Felinton.

    And now, the documentary is winning its own awards: Before being honored with the International Emmy Award, it also won a Grimme Prize, one of Germany's most prestigious television awards.

    Felinton was able to steal the film in the first place in part because when it first appeared online in 2023, it could just be downloaded from YouTube.

    Drost and Henneberg say uploading "Butty" back then wasn't a mistake, saying that was the risk of putting something online.

    The alternative would have been not to show the film at all, they remarked; then no one would have seen it.

    They have a clear message for young creatives.

    "Don't be discouraged. Be aware that something like this can happen — but stay creative in how you deal with it. Suing is expensive and often doesn't do much good. Instead, show the world that you're the authors.".

    Industry observers note that what started out as film plagiarism ended up becoming material for another project. And that's perhaps the most unusual twist in this very quirky story.

    This article was originally published in German in February 2026 and was updated on November 24, 2026, following the International Emmy Awards.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    King Charles and Elton John have paid tribute to Australian music industry legend Molly Meldrum, who died aged 83 after a long illness.

    Meldrum's family said he "passed away peacefully" at a hospital in Melbourne in the early hours of Monday morning.

    The music promoter and broadcaster, born Ian Alexander Meldrum, helped define the nation's music tastes for decades, championing local artists like INXS and Kylie Minogue and global acts like Abba.

    Known for his chaotic demeanour and trademark Stetson hat, he interviewed an array of stars, with the king on Monday calling him "a true giant of the music industry".

    Born in Victoria in 1943, Meldrum displayed a love of music from an early age and went on to host the Australian Broadcasting Corporation's music television programme Countdown, and later a segment on variety show Hey Hey, It's Saturday.

    Meldrum in 2014 became the first person who was not a recording artist to be inducted into the Australian Recording Industry Association (Aria) Hall of Fame.

    Meldrum lived with an acquired brain injury after falling from a ladder in 2011.

    "Affectionately dubbed 'the Guru', Molly was the heartbeat, the champion and the spirit of Australian music," a statement from Meldrum's family stated.

    Among his most famous interviews was a 1977 sit-down with King Charles, in which Meldrum could not calm his jitters.

    He stumbled over his lines, declaring: "Your Royal Highness... Oh, oh, I'm sweating like a pig".

    King Charles reflected on the infamous interview for Countdown's 40th anniversary special, saying: "There is an old showbusiness saying which warns never to work with animals or children. But nobody prepared me for Molly Meldrum".

    On Monday, an aide to the King said he had been "deeply saddened" to hear of Meldrum's death.

    "His Majesty's interview with Molly is a moment he and many others will never forget - he hopes that interview will once again raise a few smiles as Australians honour Molly's legacy as a true giant of the music industry.".

    Elton John - a friend and regular interviewee - paid tribute to him as "an Australian legend and an institution", while pop star Kylie Minogue said she would be turning up the music in his honour.

    "As a kid, I watched Molly Meldrum on Countdown every single weekend, in awe of the show and the magic it brought to our little TV in the lounge room.".

    According to recent reports, "He championed so many Aussie artists and welcomed international artists to Australia in his own wonderful and inimitable way. I'm so grateful for his unwavering love and support.".

    Australia's Arts Minister Tony Burke stated the country had lost an icon: "One of his greatest legacies will be the generations of Australians who grew up with his unmistakable enthusiasm and love of music.".

    Prime Minister Mark Carney brought a Donald Trump impersonator on stage at Ottawa's annual press gallery dinner, where he poked fun at strained US-Canada relations and on-again, off-again trade talks.

    The impersonator, played by comedian Mark Critch of the sketch comedy show This Hour Has 22 Minutes, came out after Carney jokingly pressed an "emergency comedy button" during his speech.

    Critch appeared alongside another actor impersonating Carney, played by Canadian sketch comedian Mark McKinney.

    "We've got two Carneys here, it's a disaster," the Trump impersonator said after he walked on stage.

    Using some of Trump's signature mannerisms, like his dance moves and his slightly hunched posture, he joked about the latest US midterm elections, which led to Trump's Republican Party losing control in Congress.

    "I'm so popular we just had a big BLUE WAVE in the states," the impersonator said at the Saturday press gala.

    He also took aim at ongoing US-Canada trade negotiations, saying,"We're going to have a great deal. There's only one thing standing in the way: me, because I'm crazy.".

    There were also jabs at Trump's search for a fresh White House press secretary following Katie Zacharia's exit, and at US ambassador to Canada Pete Hoekstra, who is unpopular among Canadians.

    "I said 'find somebody who is less likeable than me,' and we got one," the Trump impersonator joked about Hoekstra.

    Sources indicate that carney stood behind him occasionally laughing. The prime minister also delivered his own zingers, saying at one point: "This is a tough room. And I've been in the Oval Office. Alone. With its upcoming interior decorator.".

    Both Critch and McKinney - the two impersonators - are fixtures of This Hour Has 22 Minutes, a long-standing Canadian sketch comedy show that has recently enjoyed viral internet fame for its timely skits mocking the Trump administration.

    The skits, published directly on Tik Tok and YouTube, have depicted Zacharia's quick ouster, external and poked fun at rapper Nicki Minaj's, external support for Trump.

    They have garnered millions of views, and even captured the attention of major US media., external.

    Critch and McKinney's appearance at Saturday's dinner is part of an evening of traditionally light-hearted humour, where Canadian politicians poke fun at one another at a gala hosted by the Canadian Parliamentary Press Gallery.

    In a separate speech, Canada's governor general, Louise Arbour, joked about Carney's popularity and frequent global travel.

    "Our prime minister is already getting a lot of attention. Actually, I heard a guy the other day compare him to God. Now seriously, do you know the difference between God and Mark Carney? God is everywhere, and Mark Carney is everywhere except in Ottawa where he's supposed to be," Arbour said.
